_README: Copy to studies/<name>/study.json and fill it in. `/intake` writes this for
you by interview, which is the better route -- it asks the questions in an
order that surfaces what you do not know yet.
THE CONTEXT BLOCK IS THE POINT. It is how your domain reaches the model:
appended to a FIXED prompt as data, never as an edit to prompt text. That is
what lets two studies claim the same instrument, and it is checkable --
prompt_hash is identical across studies or the claim is false. A study that
omits `context` still runs, and extracts worse, silently.
Leave `final_tag` as CHANGE-ME. Lineage is not knowable until the repair
chain has run, and inventing one produces a study that reads the wrong
vocabulary. Build, read compare_vocab.py, then write the tag you settled on.
title: one line naming the dataset and the question
question: the question every analyst in this corpus was asked

CORPUS-NAME.label: how to refer to it in prose
CORPUS-NAME.glob: pattern matching ONE run directory, relative to the corpus root
_artifacts_note: A string is one filename. A LIST is candidates: the largest present
becomes that role and the runner-up becomes <role>_secondary, which is
how a corpus with two prose channels at two time points is read.
distill.py reads these -- nothing about filenames is hardcoded.
CORPUS-NAME._required_note: Roles a run must have to count at all. Default: every role in `artifacts`. Make code optional here if some runs are prose-only -- they still count as runs contributing zero decisions, which is usually a finding rather than a nuisance.
CORPUS-NAME._min_bytes_note: Per-role size floor. Default 1, i.e. merely non-empty. Raise it where a stub file would otherwise pass: an unfetched Git-LFS pointer is valid UTF-8 at about 130 bytes, and a two-line report is not a write-up.
CORPUS-NAME.arm_from_path: optional regex with one group, if runs carry an arm
CORPUS-NAME.arm: or a constant arm, when the corpus has only one

_comment: Domain context, appended to prompts as DATA. Never edit prompt text --
the cache is keyed on it, and an edit orphans every answer that wording
produced. templates/intake.md section C works through what to collect.
If a corpus seems to need the DEFINITION of a decision changed, that is a
finding about the instrument, not a configuration step. Record it and say
so; do not widen the definition here.
context.dataset: one or two sentences: what one row is, and over what period

glossary.TERM: what a reader outside the field would not know, in one line
glossary._note: field shorthand, column names, units. 3-8 entries is typical

not_decisions: operations that look like choices in this field but are conventions
e.g. loading from a fixed path, setting a seed, library imports
easily_missed_decisions: choices a non-specialist reader would skim past
these are the ones that become silent decisions if nobody names them

research_questions: what you want the map to answer
written before the build, so the study has a stated purpose

predictions._comment: Record BEFORE results. Written now, a later match is a prediction; written after, it is a story. `/intake` asks for these at section E2.
expected_to_matter: the forks you already suspect are contested
predictions.outcome: left empty until results exist, then filled in and dated

provenance._comment: Every run carries one of these. Provenance stratifies, it does not filter -- every run counts toward the statistics, and stability.py reports them with and without non-corpus runs so any drift is visible rather than silent.
provenance.corpus: extracted from an analysis a real analyst wrote
provenance.itinerary: assembled from options the corpus already contains
provenance.authored: contains an operation no run in the corpus performed

comparisons._comment: Which contrasts the design supports. Anything not listed as fair is observational, and any causal claim lives only in `fair`.

fair.between: the randomly assigned variable, if there is one

unfair.between: groups that differ in more than one way

outcomes.note: omit this block entirely if the study has no outcome side. Better absent than pointing at a file that does not exist. Ask early whether an outcome EXTRACTOR exists or must be written -- assembling outcomes outside the pipeline is how records end up with no provenance.
